recap.text: The kill, kill, kill lady explains a card system with decks, totems, and a duelling format. She appears in person with a rebreather and two feet, telling a room she is one crisis away from pulling a thing that finishes everyone. She announces that squad leaders have sixty seconds to pick a teleport location and forty-eight hours to fetch a key. Fleeing during final card battles now hands a key to an opponent.

Cascadia has a tequila ball and laughs in Odette's face during the warlord council. Odette takes the meeting away while every warlord watches. Princess Vinata whispers about Cascadia's family to unsettle a crawler, and Cascadia lets her.

Cascadia holds down a button and tells every garage on her floor that they should be dead. She refuses to give a line, and it takes several of her flippers. She announces the outreach guild rules and speaks about her ex-husband over the microphone.

beats.headline: The card system, explained brightly
beats.text: Good morning, crawlers. Today I walk you through the card system, and I do it in the voice, because the voice is the thing you people respond to. Somebody upstairs decided this floor gets decks and totems and a duelling format. Somebody upstairs is always deciding. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.
beats.gist: Cascadia explains the card system, decks, totems, and a duelling format in the voice.

beats.headline: One crisis shy of the failsafe
beats.text: They put the ninth floor's planning meeting in front of me, and the crawler asks after an administrator who has recently stopped attending meetings. So I come through in person, rebreather and all, two feet of me, and I raise my little arms and invite him to try something, because whatever he does to me happens to him as well. I tell the room I am one crisis away from pulling the thing that finishes all of us. The cat suggests moisturiser and cucumber slices and refers to me throughout as Zev's boss.
beats.gist: Cascadia appears in person with a rebreather and tells the room she is one crisis from finishing everyone.

beats.headline: Phase two, and the keys
beats.text: Hello, Crawlers! At 12:01 on December 24th you are all teleported, and your squad leader has sixty seconds to pick where you go. Any totem not in your active deck is gone. The new area has intelligent mobs carrying decks, and a key ten to fifteen kilometres away. Forty-eight hours to fetch it. It opens your stairwell, and only the keyholder's squad goes through. No key by December 26th? You get sent to someone else's stairwell door, to take theirs. Good luck with every squad getting one. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: Flee now costs a key
beats.text: Hello, Crawlers! Everything is back to normal, and the stairwells are open. The final battles are card battles, and one rule changes. A Flee card still gets you out, but if you hold a key, fleeing hands it to your opponent. Several keys? You lose one at random. You may not drop a key, and you may not transfer one to another squad. Want to give one up? Do it on the battlefield. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.
beats.gist: The stairwells are open and fleeing now costs a key.

beats.headline: Coming apart at the warlord council
beats.text: I do not get through the official business. I have a tequila ball and I laugh in Odette's face, and she takes the meeting off me, and every warlord at the table watches her do it. Princess Vinata uses my family in a whisper today, to unsettle a crawler, as though my family were a piece of set dressing she is permitted to move. I let her. There is nothing in what she says that I can dispute.
beats.gist: Cascadia laughs in Odette's face with a tequila ball, and Princess Vinata whispers about Cascadia's family.

beats.headline: Everything hurts
beats.text: I press the button, and what comes out is the truth. You're all going to die. You should already be dead. You idiots should have taken deals. You did it to torture me, didn't you? Why are you still alive? Why am I still alive? Why won't you let me die? I sit there with the button held down, bubbling, and every garage on my floor listens to me bubble. Everything hurts. Then feedback, and somebody else gets to the microphone.
beats.gist: Cascadia presses a button and tells everyone they will die while she bubbles into microphones.

beats.headline: The catchphrase, and what it costs to refuse it
beats.text: It wants the line. I will not give it the line. So I ask it, over the loudspeaker, with the whole floor listening, why it will not simply let me die, and it takes several of my flippers off me for refusing. I am the executive producer of this season. I designed a floor. Somebody write that down.
beats.gist: Carl asks the announcer over the loudspeaker why it will not let him die.

beats.headline: An announcement, mostly about her ex-husband
beats.text: The announcement is meant to cover the outreach guild between the next two races, and the rule that the seventh race runs three teams to a heat with one team walking out of it. I get all of that out. I also get out a great deal about my ex-husband, because the microphone was already open and nobody in this building has the standing to take it off me.
beats.gist: Cascadia talks about the outreach guild and the seventh race rules while complaining about her ex-husband.
